title: SRE field notes: latency spikes, fallback behavior, and handoff actions (Nov 1–7, 2027)
content:
Scope: weekly SRE field notes covering Nov 1–7, 2027. Purpose is to capture observed incidents, SLO state, temporary mitigations, runbook gaps discovered during the week, and the on-call handoff checklist for next rotation. These are rough notes — some items are ‘notes to self’ and questions for follow-up.

Summary (top-line):
- One P1 latency incident on 2027-11-03 (client-facing text-generation API) triggered by unexpected KV cache churn combined with aggressive scale-down. Customer impact: elevated 95th/99th latency for ~27 minutes, increased error rates for short tail of traffic.
- SLOs: production 99th-percentile latency SLO missed for a 30-minute window (see metrics below). No data loss, no model corruption.
- Immediate mitigation: temporary capacity floor (pinned nodes) + disabled aggressive scale-down policy for the Dedicated cluster serving model-family-alpha.
- Action items created: update autoscaler heuristics, add runbook step for cache warmup and gradual scale-down, create synthetic test that exercises tail KV-miss behavior.

Incident detail — Nov 3 P1 (KV cache churn + scale-down):
- Timeline (UTC):
  - 14:05: anomalous rise in 95th/99th latency on model-family-alpha route (alert SRE-LAT-99).
  - 14:07: first page to on-call, paged twice as latency spiked > SLO breach threshold.
  - 14:10: investigation showed high KV cache eviction rate on workers; cache hit ratio dropped from ~98% -> 57% as a background rebalancer and eviction job overlapped with scale-down.
  - 14:15: autoscaler removed 2 nodes per pool (scale-down decision based on pod-idle CPU and rack balancing), causing KV cache cold-start on the remaining nodes and temporary queueing in the request router.
  - 14:32: mitigation applied — pinned 3 nodes and increased minimum replica count for cluster.
  - 14:40: latency returned to baseline and alerts resolved by 14:42.
- Root cause hypothesis: two contributing factors: (1) a rebalancer job introduced by recent runtime PR that aggressively evicts least-recently-used KV segments during compaction; (2) our scale-down policy used a short observation window and removed nodes before the KV cache had a chance to rewarm across remaining replicas. The combinatoric overlap created a cache churn storm.
- Evidence collected: logs from runtime showing eviction spikes (logs attached to SRE-4123), autoscaler decision events, router queue length metrics. We captured kernel-level timestamps to reconstruct request queuing.

SLO snapshot and metrics (production, model-family-alpha):
- Target: 99th percentile < 1500ms for text-generation endpoint (rolling 30d).
- Week snapshot (rolling 7d):
  - Median latency: 210ms
  - P95: 840ms
  - P99: 2,060ms (breach window contribution on 2027-11-03)
  - Errors (502/timeout): spike to 0.8% for 14:05–14:35 window vs baseline 0.03%
- Cost/efficiency note: the pinned nodes doubled tail capacity cost for 3 hours; estimated incremental cost $1.2k for mitigation window. Documented in ticket SRE-4123.

Temporary mitigations applied (and why):
- Pinned minimum replicas to avoid immediate re-eviction during monitoring window. Rationale: quick way to protect warm caches while longer fixes progress.
- Disabled rebalancer compaction job on cluster variant for 24h (rollback blocked until tests pass).
- Adjusted router queue thresholds to shed low-priority background traffic during tail events (apply backpressure to best-effort routes).

Runbook issues discovered (gaps):
- No explicit runbook step for simultaneous cache-eviction + scale-down scenario; current runbook assumes cache cold-start only.
- Observability gap: eviction metrics are present but were not surfaced on on-call dashboard (heatmap missing). Need a tile showing eviction rate per node and per-shard.
- Autoscaler policy docs: window size and decision trace are not easily queryable from monitoring; need extractable audit trail for scale decisions.

Action items (owners and ETA):
- SRE-4123 (Maya): collect full timeline artifacts and draft postmortem (ETA 2027-11-12).
- Runtime team to revert/soft-disable rebalancer compaction PR while we add throttling in the job (Owner: Priya Nair, ETA 2027-11-11).
- Autoscaler tuning: increase scale-down observation window from 3m -> 10m for Dedicated clusters serving production traffic; add cooldowns after compaction jobs (Owner: Evan Park, ETA 2027-11-14).
- Observability: add eviction-rate heatmap to SRE dashboard and include autoscaler decision traces (Owner: Jonah Kim, ETA 2027-11-16).
- Add a synthetic test that blasts a route to artificially stress KV distribution and measure warmup time (Owner: Maya, ETA 2027-11-18).

On-call handoff checklist (explicit tasks for incoming shift):
- Review SRE-4123 status and whether pinned-node mitigation is still necessary. If pinned nodes > baseline, evaluate safe rollback steps with runtime team.
- Verify eviction heatmap exists and displays current cluster state before 09:00 local shift start.
- Confirm autoscaler cool-down flags are set (ask infra-automation oncall if needed).
- Validate scheduled compaction jobs are disabled for affected model-family for the next 24h.
- Check for follow-up alerts: SRE-LAT-99, SRE-AUTOSCALE-ERR, SRE-KVCACHE-LOSS. Acknowledge and annotate any recurring alerts.
- Notes to incoming oncall: pay special attention to router queue length spikes rather than only token-per-second metrics — queue length was earliest leading indicator in this incident.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider adding a "cache-rewarm grace window" annotation to the autoscaler: after any job that does compaction/eviction, autoscaler should enter a supervised state where scale-down decisions are conservative for N minutes.
- Explore change where eviction jobs check cluster-wide load and defer operations if tail latency > threshold. Work with runtime to add these checks.

Open questions / discussion items for next SRE sync:
- How to surface per-shard KV eviction rates without overwhelming metrics cardinality? (options: sampled metrics, centralized shard aggregator).
- What is a reasonable cost budget for pinned-node mitigations in future incidents? Do we have an on-call-spend approval flow?
- Should we add a special SLO for 'cache-availability' (e.g., fraction of requests served from warm-KV) as a leading indicator for latency SLOs?

Relevant links and tickets: SRE-4123 (incident ticket), SRE-4130 (autoscaler tuning epic), https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/kv-cache-eviction-postmortem, runtime PR 876 (rebalancer compaction), slack thread #ops-incidents (link above).

Appendix — quick checklist for postmortem draft:
- Attach timeline artifacts (router queues, node eviction logs, autoscaler events).
- Diagram pre-incident vs post-incident topology (which nodes removed).
- Cost impact summary (include pinned-node cost).
- Proposed permanent mitigations and rollout plan (autoscaler policy change, compaction throttling, monitoring tiles).
- Stakeholder notification plan (GTM + CS + affected customers).

If anything else comes up overnight add to this doc and ping the triage channel. — M.D.
